Consult Summary:
- Acute chest discomfort with associated symptoms raises concern for possible acute coronary syndrome; ambulance requested for prehospital evaluation and ECG.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Chest pressure described as “pressure on chest,” felt during gardening a couple of hours ago; symptoms persist. Palpitations reported. Nausea with sweating and shortness of breath.
- Onset/duration: Started a couple of hours ago; ongoing.
- Progression: Symptoms currently present; no explicit improvement.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Occurred with non-strenuous activity (gardening); no relief noted.
- Associated symptoms: Palpitations (heart beating faster), sweating, mild nausea, shortness of breath.
- Context: Gardening at home; not during heavy exercise.
- ROS relevant positive/negative: Positive for chest pressure, left arm/shoulder pain, dyspnea, diaphoresis, palpitations; negative specifics not documented beyond not vomiting.
- Past medical history: Hypertension; overweight; smoker; no diabetes; cholesterol status not checked.
- Medications: None listed; medication reconciliation not documented.
- Allergies: Aspirin allergy with mild allergic reaction (swelling); patient notes this allergy.
- Social history: Lives alone; restaurant owner (sushi shop); smokes about 10 cigarettes/day for 15 years; alcohol use ~7–8 pints per week; generally low activity.
- Family history: Father died of a heart attack around age 60; mother had heart problems.
- Date of birth: August 8, 1958 (transcript states birth in 1958); age estimates within conversation were inconsistent (patient’s approximate age around sixty vs clinician’s earlier estimate around fifty-one).
- Relevant negatives/uncertainties: No prior history of similar symptoms; no diabetes; no prior cholesterol checks.

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension.
- Overweight.
- Smoker: ~10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years.
- Family history: Father with premature heart disease (died of heart attack around age 60); mother with heart problems.
- Diabetes and cholesterol status: Not diabetic; cholesterol not checked.

Medications:
- None listed. (Dose/route/frequency not documented.)

Allergies:
- Aspirin allergy with mild swelling reaction; dose/route/trigger not documented.

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Occupation: Sushi restaurant owner.
- Smoking: 10 cigarettes/day for 15 years.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints/week.
- Activity: Generally low physical activity.
- Financial/lifestyle factors: Not otherwise documented beyond occupation and home situation.

Family History:
- Father: Heart attack around age 60.
- Mother: Heart problems noted.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not provided.
- Examination findings: Not described.

Investigations:
- Prehospital ECG planned by ambulance; ECG performed by ambulance team upon arrival.
- Plan indicates transfer decisions based on ECG and clinical assessment.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Possible acute coronary syndrome (ACS) presenting with chest pressure, left arm/shoulder pain, diaphoresis, and dyspnea.
  - Plan:
    - Ambulance activation and prehospital ECG (to be performed by ambulance staff).
    - Transfer to hospital for further ACS assessment based on ECG and clinical status.
    - I will remain on the line with the patient until ambulance arrives; handover to EMS with details.
    - Ensure access: front door remains open for EMS; patient will be reassessed in hallway if needed.
- Issue 2: Aspirin allergy.
  - Plan:
    - Document aspirin allergy clearly and inform hospital/EMS.
    - Note to hospital that aspirin allergy may be present and that aspirin use may be reconsidered; decision to use aspirin will depend on hospital assessment.
- Issue 3: Risk factors for cardiovascular disease.
  - Plan:
    - Acknowledge hypertension, smoking, overweight, and positive family history as contributing risk factors.
    - No specific outpatient management plan documented yet; management will be determined by ED/EMS and subsequent care.
- General:
  - Reinforce safety: Do not drive; call ambulance; door access arranged; continue to monitor status and be available for EMS handover.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Vital signs not documented; full physical examination not provided; current medications list not documented; no ECG results or cardiac enzyme labs available in this note.
- Internal conflicts: Age estimation conflict noted — patient states birth year 1958 (age ~60s) while clinician previously estimated around fifty-something.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; minor conversational noise with some back-and-forth about age. No audio ambiguity affecting critical clinical content.
